nodes.description: Both ATP9A alleles carry nonsense, frameshift-causing or canonical splice-site variants. In patient fibroblasts ATP9A mRNA falls to a few percent of control levels, consistent with nonsense-mediated decay, so little or no ATP9A flippase is made. ATP9A is a P4-ATPase whose ATPase activity is stimulated by negatively charged phospholipids such as phosphatidylserine and phosphoinositides.

nodes.description: ATP9A sits in phosphatidylserine-positive early and recycling endosomes. Its depletion delays transferrin recycling and traps the glucose transporter GLUT1 in endosomes, while early-to-late endosomal transport and retrograde transport to the Golgi are spared. In neuronal cells and mouse brain, ATP9A loss lowers the active GTP-bound forms of RAB5 and RAB11, and patient truncating mutants mislocalize.

evidence.reference_title: The phospholipid flippase ATP9A is required for the recycling pathway from the endosomes to the plasma membrane.
evidence.snippet: Moreover, depletion of ATP9A caused accumulation of glucose transporter 1 in endosomes, probably by inhibiting their recycling.

evidence.snippet: It mainly localizes to endosomes and plays a pivotal role in endosomal recycling pathway by modulating small GTPase RAB5 and RAB11 activation.

nodes.description: ATP9A forms a conserved complex with MON2 and DOPEY2 that associates with SNX3-retromer, which retrieves the Wnt cargo receptor Wntless from endosomes. In C. elegans, loss of the ATP9A orthologue degrades Wntless and perturbs Wnt signaling. Whether Wnt secretion is reduced in patient neurons, and whether this contributes to the human phenotype, has not been tested.

evidence.reference_title: SNX3-retromer requires an evolutionary conserved MON2:DOPEY2:ATP9A complex to mediate Wntless sorting and Wnt secretion.
evidence.snippet: Here we demonstrate the essential role of SNX3-retromer assembly for Wntless transport and report that SNX3 associates with an evolutionary conserved endosome-associated membrane re-modelling complex composed of MON2, DOPEY2 and the putative aminophospholipid translocase, ATP9A.

evidence.reference_title: SNX3-retromer requires an evolutionary conserved MON2:DOPEY2:ATP9A complex to mediate Wntless sorting and Wnt secretion.
